government.note: Federal presidential republic under the 1988 Constitution. The President is head of state and of government, elected with the Vice President on a joint ticket by two-round popular vote for a four-year term; a 1997 constitutional amendment allows one consecutive re-election. The National Congress has two chambers: the Chamber of Deputies (513, open-list proportional representation by state) and the Federal Senate (81, three per state and Federal District, eight-year terms renewed alternately by one third and two thirds every four years). The Vice President succeeds on a vacancy. Impeachment is authorised by the Chamber of Deputies and tried by the Senate; the President is suspended while the Senate trial runs (Dilma Rousseff, 12 May to 31 August 2016, removed).

system.note: Open-list proportional representation in 27 multi-member constituencies (the 26 states and the Federal District) of 8 to 70 seats; integer quotients, with remaining seats by the D'Hondt method. Party federations (since 2022) run as a single list.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the October 1998 Chamber of Deputies vote: PSDB 17.54% (third way), PFL 17.30%, PPB 11.35% and PTB 5.66% (liberal conservative, 34.3%), PMDB 15.17% (big tent), PT 13.19% (split evenly between social democrat and democratic socialist, reflecting its then socialist programme), PDT 5.67%, PSB 3.41% and PPS 1.31% (social democrat), PL 2.47% and PSL 0.27% (classical liberal), PCdoB 1.30% (Marxist-Leninist), PRONA 0.89% (national conservative), PSC 0.67% (Christian conservative), PV 0.44% (green); the remaining small parties are spread over big tent and the left. Cardoso was re-elected in the first round in 1998 with 53.06% to Lula's 31.71% and Ciro Gomes's 10.97%.
